name: Bab Bou Jeloud
hero_subtitle: The famous Blue Gate, and the easiest place to begin your walk into the medina.

overview.title: The Gate Everyone Photographs
overview.p1: Bab Bou Jeloud is the grand entrance to Fes el-Bali and its most recognisable landmark. The gate was built in the early 20th century and is faced in blue zellige on the outside and green on the inside, colours associated with Fes and with Islam. Its tall arch frames the minaret of the nearby Bou Inania madrasa.
overview.p2: Just inside, two main lanes begin, Talaa Kebira and Talaa Seghira, and the square is lined with cafés and restaurants that are lively all day. Come at dusk for the best photos as the gate lights up, or early in the morning when it is almost empty. It is a handy meeting point before you head into the medina.

1.title: The Blue Gate
1.desc: Blue on the outside, green within. Best photographed at dusk or early in the morning.

2.title: Terrace Cafés
2.desc: Grab a terrace table for mint tea and watch the flow of people through the gate.

3.title: Talaa Kebira & Talaa Seghira
3.desc: Two main lanes start just inside and lead down through the medina, past madrasas and souks.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Bab Bou Jeloud

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Petit taxis stop right outside the gate, which makes it the easiest entry point. Agree on the meter before you set off.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Come at dusk when the gate is lit, or early morning when it is nearly empty. Midday is busy and hot.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Expect touts offering to guide you. A polite no is enough, and agree prices before accepting any help. Keep bags closed in the crowd.

q1.question: Why is Bab Bou Jeloud called the Blue Gate?
q1.answer: Its outer face is covered in blue zellige, the colour of Fes. The inner face is green.

q2.question: When is the best time to photograph the gate?
q2.answer: At dusk, when it is lit, or early morning when there are fewer people.

q3.question: Is it free to visit?
q3.answer: Yes, the gate and the square are open and free all day.

q4.question: Where does the medina walk start?
q4.answer: Right here: Talaa Kebira and Talaa Seghira begin just inside the gate.
